That's how/why I made /v/CrazyTheories. I had an idea for a post that didn't seem to fit anywhere, so I made the sub for that post. Thanks to /v/all I ended up with almost 100 subscribers then realized 'Shit, now I have to do take care of this place'.
I like to think that's how a lot of moderators on Voat got started: see a need, fill a need, figure out the rest along the way.

figure out the rest along the way.

That's been the driving philosophy of my life.

Voat's community tends to view /all pretty regularly, and I often see small subs pop up out of nowhere as a result, which I think is awesome. I think part of the reason is that Voat gives users the ability to block subs they aren't interested in, which makes /all more useful on Voat than on Reddit. With Voat, you have the ability to filter content by whitelist (front page) and blacklist (/v/all), so you get to enjoy the advantages of both.
Which is awesome, because I found /all/new on Reddit to be completely unusable.

I think part of it is a size issue, a tools issues, and a culture issue.

  • Size: Reddit has a lot more junk moving through its /all, so a small but interesting sub gets lost in the shuffle.
  • Tools: Reddit doesn't let you curate your view of /all by blocking subs you're not interested in
  • Culture: I expect most users on Reddit stick to their subscribed subs, since most of what floats to the top is from already-popular subs. It's harder for a small sub to reach that critical mass to break out of /new. I see small subs pop up in Voat's /all fairly regularly, so it's more useful for both subverse discovery and content discovery as a result.

Edit: Another unrelated thought is that Voat has /v/Whatever as a good resource for uncategorized content, which has a good amount of subscribers. That means anyone can throw a thought into /v/Whatever and it can sink or swim on its own merit, rather than being hindered by being in a small sub.

There are a lot of simple but powerful features that make Voat great and give it value beyond just being a Reddit alternative. /v/Whatever, open mod logs, subverse blocking in /v/All, even the comment preview button before you click "submit".
And the best part is that the little unknown sub got some exposure, some lively discussion, and the chance to thrive if the concept resonates with people. It's a very democratic feeling :)
